sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Non-Dilutive Revenue-Based Financing for Digital Brands

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic codified continental system; unitary national corporate law with direct EU law application)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Over 100 active bilateral investment treaties (BITs) of France, including France–China BIT (1984) and France–United States Tax Treaty (1994)
More than 120 double taxation avoidance agreements (DTAAs) following OECD/UN Model standards
EU internal market and trade agreements (EU Treaties, EU–third-country FTAs) applicable as French law

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF) Articles L.561-1 et seq., L.561-2-2, L.561-45 to L.561-49, R.561-1 to R.561-32 and L.562-1 to L.562-16; décret n°2016-567 of 10 May 2016 as amended by décret n°2020-115 of 12 February 2020, implementing Directive (EU) 2015/849 (4AMLD) and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD); UBO register operated electronically by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) since 1 January 2020; FATF Recommendations 24 and 25 (transparency and beneficial ownership); EU Council and UN financial sanctions applicable with direct effect in France.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Commercial Register Extract of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry or company registrar of the shareholder's state of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Hague Convention of 5 October 1961, in force in France since 24 January 1965); Consular Legalization for non-Contracting States

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (certificat de bonne tenue ou de non-faillite) of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry, tax authority, or licensed registered agent of the state of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency identifying the current directors and indirect beneficial owners of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent, law firm, or competent authority of the state of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate Power of Attorney for signature of the SARL constitutional documentation (procuration pour constitution de société)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Legal representatives of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization when executed in public form outside France

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation of each apostilled document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Expert translator approved by a French Cour d'appel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No separate apostille; sworn translation accompanies the apostilled original

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence (EDD) on Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined by Article R.561-18 CMF for every counterparty, UBO, director, and beneficial recipient of royalty financing flows; screening against (i) EU Council consolidated financial sanctions list, (ii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, (iii) French national freezing/terrorist designations, and (iv) OFAC SDN List as a practical compliance benchmark for USD-denominated settlement; written AML/CFT risk assessment and customer due diligence file to be established before incorporation; STR filing duty (déclaration de soupçon) to TRACFIN under Article L.561-15 CMF for any cash or wire flow reaching the EUR 10,000 statutory threshold per client and for all suspicious structured transactions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique électronique des formalités d'entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, routing all constitutional filings to the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) held by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office's jurisdiction.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All mandatory corporate documents must be drafted in French (Article L.223-1 and Article D.123-2 Code de commerce); the selected corporate name must be expressed in Latin characters; names composed in non-Latin alphabets must be fully transliterated into Latin script; a French translation of a foreign-language name must be inserted in the objects clause of the articles of association; the name must not be misleading, offensive, or create a likelihood of confusion with an existing registered company, trademark, or notorious mark.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Établissement de crédit / Société de financement (requires prior ACPR authorization)
Assurance / Mutuelle / Réassurance (requires supervisory approval and specific legal form)
Fonds de pension / Fonds de placement / OPCVM (investment fund terminology subject to AMF licensing)
République / Ministère / Préfecture / Mairie / Police / Gendarmerie / Officiel (public authority and sovereign state tokens prohibited)
Chambre de commerce / Chambre des métiers / Ordre / Barreau (regulated order and professional body tokens prohibited)
France / Française (accepted only with substantiated national anchoring; automatically scrutinized by the Greffe)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a statutory name-reservation system; the name is secured only upon final RCS registration or upon earlier INPI trademark filing. Rejection may occur during the Greffe's formal review of the constitutional dossier. SOP upon rejection: (1) request the written statement of reasons from the Greffier within 8 calendar days; (2) file an administrative appeal (recours gracieux) before the juge commis à la surveillance du registre within 15 days of notification pursuant to décret n°84-406 of 30 May 1984, Article 24; (3) alternatively, amend the name and re-file the complete incorporation dossier through the INPI Guichet unique as a de novo filing, with priority treatment requested; (4) if the refusal is based on a prior identical trademark, initiate opposition or coexistence negotiation before INPI under Article L.712-4 CPI. A rejected name cannot be reserved or extended.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for an unlicensed commercial SARL under French law: the registered office may be a domiciliation address supplied by a commercial domiciliary company holding the prefectoral approval required by Article L.123-11-3 Code de commerce. For an ISIC 6499 revenue-based financing fund, the ACPR, DGFiP, and TRACFIN may challenge a purely virtual presence if the activity develops collection or lending-like functions; recommended structure is an approved domiciliation provider combined with a physical sub-service agreement and a local correspondence and bookkeeping base.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: estimated 5–10% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by DGFiP, URSSAF, or ACPR during the first 12 months for an unlicensed financing vehicle; the probability rises to approximately 20–30% if the company claims reduced tax leakage on cross-border royalty flows, if TRACFIN receives a suspicious transaction report, or if the registered office remains purely virtual without any operational activity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting of SARL Articles of Association (statuts) and pre-filing compliance review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent French corporate law firm (cabinet d'avocats)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing French market benchmark EUR 800–1,800 fixed fee for a standard SARL; no statutory tariff applicable

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS incorporation and constitutional filing fee through INPI Guichet unique
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory regulated tariff of EUR 27.75 pursuant to Article A.743-1 et seq. Code de commerce

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the constitutional notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French legal gazette (journal d'annonces légales) of the department of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated price band under décret n°92-496 of 2 June 1992; Paris metropolitan market rate EUR 150–220 per publication

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Approved commercial domiciliation service for 12 months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Domiciliation company approved by the Préfet (Article L.123-11-3 Code de commerce)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 20–40 per month, prepaid annually; no statutory tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) initial registration and first-year maintenance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: GLEIF-accredited Local Operating Unit (e.g., LSEG / GMEI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: LOU tariff on a competitive market basis; EUR 85 typical first-year fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation name and trademark conflict clearance search
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French corporate law firm; INPI public database access is free
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a professional conflict opinion on INPI and commercial databases; approximate EUR 80

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and sworn French translation of two foreign corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authorities of the document's state of origin and a translator approved by a French Cour d'appel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille fees fixed by the issuing state at EUR 20–50 per document; sworn translation at EUR 40–60 per page; approximate EUR 110 for two documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official K-bis extract and certified copies of registration documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff of EUR 3.85 per extract

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 governing Sociétés à Responsabilité Limitée; general company provisions under Articles 1832 et seq. of the Civil Code; RCS registration under Articles L.123-1 et seq. of the Code de commerce and Décret n°84-406 of 30 April 1984.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce in the jurisdiction of the registered office, acting as the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through the national Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises operated by INPI.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire M0 (déclaration de constitution de société) together with the executed articles of association (statuts constitutifs), transmitted electronically via the Guichet Unique formalities portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies (Code de commerce, Article L.223-2); the capital is freely determined in the articles. At least 20% of cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked escrow bank account in the name of the company in formation before the registration filing, and the balance must be paid up within five years. The deposited funds are released to the gérant only after RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
UNANIMOUS FIRST CORPORATE RESOLUTION OF [FR_SARL]
Effective upon registration by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, the shareholders of FR_SARL resolve:
1. The subscriptions to the share capital are accepted as set out in the articles of association; cash contributions will remain in the blocked escrow account until the company is legally registered.
2. The registered office is fixed at [address], France.
3. The articles of association are adopted with powers of management conferred on the gérant.
4. [Name] is appointed sole gérant, with authority to execute contracts, run the revenue-based financing business, and complete all RCS, publication, and administrative formalities.
Done at Paris, [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Parties themselves / optional notary; subsequent submission via INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the French-language statuts containing the mandatory legal clauses: corporate form, name, purpose, registered office, share capital, cash and in-kind contributions, governance powers of the gérant, distribution rules, and audit thresholds. Each shareholder must sign the final pages and initial every page. Each gérant must sign a separate acceptance act (acte de candidature).
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association (statuts constitutifs)
Passport or national identity card of each shareholder
Manager acceptance letter and specimen signature
Beneficial owner declaration (déclaration de bénéficiaire effectif)
Proof of right to occupy the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a mandatory clause is missing, execute a supplemental act (avenant) signed by all shareholders and annex it to the original file before submitting the M0 form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a blocked deposit account and escrow of share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A French credit institution supervised by the ACPR, or a notary holding client funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary 'compte bloqué' in the name of the SARL in formation. Deposit at least 20% of the cash capital (or 100% if the articles so provide). Obtain the bank's attestation de dépôt de fonds, which identifies the depositor, beneficiary, amount, and blocked status. Retain this attestation for inclusion in the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Signed articles of association
Identity document of the depositor and proposed manager
Bank opening and AML/KYC forms
Beneficial owner declaration for the bank's due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account for KYC reasons, use another credit institution or transfer the amount to a notary's escrow account and obtain a new attestation. The blocked funds are released only after production of the RCS registration certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal incorporation notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An approved legal announcements newspaper (journal d'annonces légales) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a JAL to publish a notice stating the corporate form, name, capital, registered office, purpose, duration, managers, and the commercial court with which the company will be registered. Obtain the publisher's certificate of publication. The publication must occur before or contemporaneously with the submission of the incorporation dossier.
required_dossiers: Draft notice text approved by the shareholders
Identity document of the person giving the instruction
Basic corporate information and election of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice contains errors, require the JAL to issue a corrective addendum and attach the correction to the incorporation file; if the publisher fails, select another authorized journal and republish.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the M0 incorporation dossier via the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), transmitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create an account on the official portal, select 'création d’une société à responsabilité limitée', complete the M0 declaration, upload all required dossiers, and pay the registry fee online. The Guichet performs formal completeness checks and transmits the file to the competent greffe for RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Signed articles of association (statuts constitutifs)
Bank attestation de dépôt de fonds
Certificate of legal announcement publication
Form M0 (déclaration de constitution de société)
Manager acceptance letter and identity documents
Beneficial owner declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet or greffe queries the file, respond within the statutory deadline through the online dashboard, correct the stated deficiencies, and resubmit the amended document. If the portal rejects the file, re-file a corrected M0 without additional delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and issuance of the Kbis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Greffe du Tribunal Judiciaire for certain activities) as RCS registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the M0 file from the Guichet Unique, the greffe reviews the legal conformity of the company, allocates the RCS number and SIREN/SIRET identifiers, and issues the Kbis extract evidencing legal existence. The Kbis is delivered electronically and is available via the official INPI/Infogreffe databases.
required_dossiers: Guichet Unique submission receipt and file acknowledgement
Original attestation de dépôt de fonds
Legal announcement publication certificate
Proof of the registered office address
Copy of the signed articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffe refuses registration, it must state its reasons; the applicant may cure the deficiencies in a supplementary filing or challenge the refusal before the competent judicial court via summary proceedings (référé).

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DGFiP tax office, URSSAF, social security authorities, and the selected French bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Kbis is issued, complete the operational activation: open the permanent commercial bank account, release the escrow funds by presenting the Kbis to the bank, ensure tax numbers and VAT registration are active, notify or register with URSSAF for the gérant and any employees, subscribe to insurance, and comply with any commercial lease conditions.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract
Attestation de dépôt de fonds for fund release
Bank account opening and signature cards
Commercial lease or occupancy document
Insurance certificates (civil liability, premises)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax numbers are not updated within the standard period, request activation directly from DGFiP or through the SIRENE portal; if the bank refuses the permanent account, reopen with another institution using the Kbis evidence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - the entity is engaged in non-dilutive revenue-based financing and requires no industrial or manufacturing authorization. The only administrative authority for business activity is the RCS registrar; the ACPR is not required absent regulated banking, consumer credit, or payment-service activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Ordinary RCS registration certificate (Kbis) is sufficient to operate; no separate sectoral operating permit is required under the specified business scope.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique / DREAL (Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - administrative office premises; not an ICPE (Installation classée pour la protection de l'environnement); no full EIA report required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge or VOC emission thresholds apply; the site must only comply with general waste management, waste sorting, WEEE recycling, and tertiary-building energy efficiency obligations under the Environmental Code and the Grenelle regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire-safety certification is required if the premises are not open to the public and are not classed as an ICPE. The employer must still maintain a workplace risk assessment, keep a single safety register, inspect electrical installations, install appropriate fire-detection and emergency measures, and comply with labor-code structural and accessibility standards for employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) of the French Ministry of Economy, Finance and Recovery; online portals: impots.gouv.fr for corporate tax/VAT filings and formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique) for entity and tax registration; VAT number validation via VIES (europa.eu/taxation_customs/vies).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a domestically incorporated SARL, the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) completes the single registration dossier within 24-48 hours, which triggers simultaneous issuance of: (i) SIREN and SIRET codes by INSEE; (ii) APE/NAF classification code; (iii) intra-Community VAT number (TVA intracommunautaire) by the competent Centre de Finances Publiques (CFE); and (iv) EORI number for customs if export/import activity is declared. Foreign entities with a permanent establishment or a direct registration obligation in France must appoint an accredited fiscal representative in the case of non-EU established suppliers, and file Form No. 13700 (France’s non-resident VAT registration form or the EU One-Stop-Shop route for distance sales). The VAT number is generally issued within 1-2 weeks of the dossier being complete.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (SARL is by default taxable to French corporation tax — Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS — on its worldwide profit at the ordinary 25% rate; the territorial scope rule limits taxation to profits attributable to a French permanent establishment; a SARL under specific conditions of small size and management may elect partnership-like pass-through treatment under Impôt sur le Revenu (IR), but the debt-fund activity described under ISIC 6499 in practice remains subject to IS, and revenue-based financing income would be taxed as banking/commercial income, not as capital gains relief assets).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a US-style check-the-box classification. The available elections are: (i) option for IR under Article 239 bis AA of the French General Tax Code (CGI) for small SARLs (less than 5 employees, turnover under the thresholds set by Article 50-0 CGI) — rarely suitable for an active financing fund; (ii) election for group fiscal consolidation (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI if the SARL is a 95% or more French-DGFiP resident subsidiary of a French consolidating parent (allows offsetting losses group-wide and restriction of foreign credit); (iii) approval-based election to obtain the status of ’jeune entreprise innovante’ (JEI) or ’société de financement’ for refinancing vehicles, which can affect the taxation of certain financial instruments; (iv) for hybrid instruments (e.g., revenue-based financing modelled as a redeemable preference interest), the documentation must respect the attribution rule of Article 212 bis CGI (interest deduction) and the hybrid mismatch rules transposing ATAD that disallow a double non-taxation result; no conversion from IS to IR is possible after 5 years of existence.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée — TVA) under Article 256 CGI; intra-Community and non-Community provisions harmonised with Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 for a French-resident SARL: VAT registration and chargeability commence with the first taxable transaction (no de minimis threshold for corporations). For non-EU-established suppliers, the distance-sales and electronic-services union threshold is EUR 10,000; above this, VAT must be charged in France or declared via the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) / Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) schemes. As a pure financial intermediaire, the SARL typically falls under the VAT exemption of Articles 261 C 1° CGI (lending, credit intermediation, debt factoring), thus no output VAT is chargeable on its revenue-based financing income; input tax recovery is proportionally restricted under the feeder-of-exempt-services prorata rule.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B e-invoicing in France is being deployed through the national e-invoicing reform (Loi de Finances 2020, implemented by the DGFiP, with a three-phase timetable: 1 September 2026 for large taxpayers, 1 September 2027 for SMEs, 1 September 2027 for all domestic B2B transactions; foreign suppliers operate via the central platform) — mandatory E-reporting to DGFiP for all cross-border B2C and B2B inter-Community transactions, with digital transmission via an accredited Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) or the public free portal Chorus Pro. There is no ’real-time clearance’ in the Latin American sense; the French mandate requires near-real-time E-reporting (within 30 minutes for B2B invoices once the reform is operational) and the issuance of invoices in a structured e-invoicing format (Factur-X/UBL/CII) with a mandatory electronic signature for fiscal integrity, but no physical digital stamp. For export VAT refund claims, the DGFiP may require digital certification of the exporter’s shipping and customs declarations via the DELTA-T/SIGL (Système d’Information de la Douane).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under French VAT law, exports of goods to a non-EU destination are taxable at 0% (Article 262-I-1 CGI) where the exporter proves that the goods actually left the EU within the legal deadline and are held by the buyer outside the EU. Intra-Community dispatches to an EU taxable person are zero-rated under Article 262-I-2 CGI if the buyer communicates a valid EU VAT ID, the buyer’s supplier files an EC sales list, and the goods are transported to the other Member State. For ’offshore’ services (services subcontracted for the needs of export sales, transport, handling and brokerage related to export goods), Article 262-I-3 CGI extends zero-rating to certain ancillary services. For this SARL’s core ISIC 6499 activity — revenue-based financing of digital brands — the service is a financial credit operation that is exempt from VAT (with credit deduction) rather than zero-rated; zero-rating does not apply to pure financing. The only path to zero-rating for this entity would be if the financing service is demonstrably tied to, and invoiced as part of, an export-merchandising service package (fees for arranging the export of goods). Claiming 0% on a financial service not eligible for zero-rating can constitute an abusive VAT practice under Article 266 CGI and the ’Ashworth’ type case law (CJEU).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d’Exportation via the DELTA/T import-export software, accepted by Customs and printed as the EX1 or EX7 control document)
Bill of Lading (for sea freight) or Air Waybill (for air freight) and the corresponding Transport Contract with pickup language confirming delivery to the final non-EU destination

Inward Remittance Certificate — bank statement or SWIFT credit confirmation proving that the export proceeds are received in France or on the exporter’s account, in conformity with the currency restrictions of Article L. 161-2 of the French Monetary and Financial Code
Proof of commercial character — supplier’s order, commercial invoice, packing list, and insurance certificate aligning consignee, value, and INCOTERM
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP Audit National des Opérations Internationales (AONI) and the French Customs Anti-Fraud Office (DNRED) target export zero-rating refunds, applying the following penalties: (i) a 40% ’manquement délibéré’ (deliberate negligence) penalty plus monthly 0.4% late-payment interest (Article 1727 CGI) where the taxpayer cannot substantiate the export; (ii) a 80% ’mauvaise foi’ or ’abus de droit’ penalty, increased to 80% + 40% in cases of fraud (escroquerie à la TVA) with potential criminal prosecution for tax fraud (Article 1741 CGI) carrying up to 5 years imprisonment and EUR 250,000 fine; (iii) retrospective VAT clawback of the incorrectly zero-rated VAT and reversal of all net VAT credits for the period; (iv) an asset freeze and seizure, plus personal joint liability of the SARL manager under Article 266 bis CGI for deliberate non-payment; (v) the obligation to produce a bank guarantee for further refunds under Article 287 CGI where a fraud risk is detected. In addition, France strictly enforces the FX repatriation rule under Articles L. 211-36 and L. 231-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code: export proceeds must be repatriated and converted by the due date of the contract (subject to the default 180 days in cross-border practice, but the applicable statutory deadline is the maturity date of the invoice; any extension beyond statutory limits requires the exporter to produce an invoice maturity report). Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the legal deadline attracts a fine of up to 5% of the non-repatriated amount under Article 459 of the Customs Code.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) as national central bank of the French Republic under the European System of Central Banks (ESCB); banking and financial supervision for prudential and anti-money-laundering purposes is exercised concurrently by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR); foreign-exchange policy, balance-of-payments statistics, and financial sanctions administration sit with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) within the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté Industrielle et Numérique.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a Eurozone member; the euro is fully convertible and free transferability of capital is guaranteed under Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and Articles L151-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code Monétaire et Financier, CMF). There are no residual exchange controls on current or capital account. Profit and dividend remittances are legally unrestricted, but each payment flow must satisfy (i) corporate documentation and any applicable French withholding tax reporting (Form 2777 for sums paid to non-residents), (ii) bank due-diligence and source-of-funds verification, and (iii) EU and French sanctions, embargo, and asset-freeze compliance. Statistical reporting to the Banque de France and customs disclosure to the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) apply only at identified thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender regime or mandatory conversion ratio applies in France. A French exporter may retain foreign-currency receipts or convert them freely in the interbank market; however, all export proceeds must be routed through a financial institution established in the European Economic Area for balance-of-payments statistical purposes, and no remittance may materially benefit a sanctioned person or entity under EU Regulation 269/2014 and CMF Articles L151-1 to L165-1.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Treasury Account
Operational Treasury Account / FX Hedging Counterparty

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole CIB (Corporate and Investment Banking)
CIC (Crédit Industriel et Commercial, Groupe Crédit Mutuel)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Medium - legal feasibility is confirmed. PSD2-authorised Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto, Shine (Groupe Société Générale), and comparable EU EMIs holding licences from the ACPR, BaFin, or the FCA with EU passporting rights may open EUR IBAN escrow and collection accounts and support SEPA Instant and SWIFT credit transfers. They are, however, not a complete cross-border treasury clearing rail: they generally do not offer commercial letters of credit, FX forwards or NDFs, nostro multi-currency settlement, or sophisticated trade-payment interfaces, and enhanced due-diligence review of a non-dilutive royalty-financing fund model may trigger sub-limits, lower velocity tolerances, and longer onboarding timelines.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of at least one corporate officer, classically the manager (gérant) of the SARL, at the bank's French branch is the default commercial practice under the ACPR know-your-client expectations in CMF Articles L561-5 to L561-7. The majority of tier-1 French banks require in-person identity verification of signatories and ultimate beneficial owners at account opening. Since 2019, remote video-identification in French or English has become acceptable to several institutions provided that (i) original corporate documents are apostilled or legalised and certified, (ii) the Registre National des Entreprises beneficial-owner extract is filed, (iii) a French registered office exists, and (iv) a local agent or a French-qualified lawyer is available to attend an in-person interview if the enhanced-risk assessment so requires. Non-resident directors without any French nexus will typically be asked to appoint an approved local intermediary responsible for the banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unidentifiable ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) behind the SARL's royalty-financing structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) UBO declaration extract; notarised and apostilled shareholder register; audited ownership chain diagram; notarised identity documents of all natural-person UBOs; written confirmation that the entity is not a shell under EU AMLD5/AMLD6 criteria; management resume and sanction-clearance report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border inbound capital injection from a non-resident shareholder or a foreign alternative investment vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly executed Subscription or Shareholder Loan Agreement with audit trail; DGDDI Form 2561 declaration if aggregate foreign borrowings exceed EUR 50,000; source-of-wealth statement for injecting parties; bank references from the remitting jurisdiction; commercial rationale memorandum evidencing the non-dilutive revenue-based financing model; board resolution approving the capital injection and treasury mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty collections and disbursement footprints touching higher-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Licence and royalty agreement registry; downstream licensee KYC files; commercial due-diligence annexes to each periodic disbursement; sanctions screening logs aligned to EU Regulation 269/2014; territorial exclusion policy expressly excluding Crimea, Syria, Belarus, Iran, North Korea, and any Russian-occupied region; written confirmation from the French registered compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High volume and velocity of inbound royalty financing repayments creating a mixed-funds or layering audit risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contractually documented non-dilutive royalty waterfall; monthly investor and lending subscription listing; fully reconciled capital account and escrow ledger; ISIC 6499 revenue-based-financing advisory opinion; internal control memo on segregation of client funds; independent audit report of a Commissaire aux Comptes where statutory thresholds are exceeded.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of local economic substance and administration by non-resident directors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French registered-office lease contract; designation of an approved local legal or tax advisor; board minutes resolving treasury-account opening and signatory powers; professional indemnity insurance certificate; director curriculum vitae and global sanction-clearance evidence; commitment to maintain local books and records for French corporate income tax and DAC6 reporting.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections, being share capital increases, shareholder loans, or tranches of the non-dilutive financing fund, must be routed via SWIFT MT103 or TARGET2 euro-denominated credit transfer, quoting the relevant ISO 20022 purpose code (LOAN for shareholder financing, INVS for investment capital) and attaching or referencing the executed financing instrument. Any aggregate foreign-currency borrowing contracted by the French resident SARL exceeding EUR 50,000 must be declared to the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) on Form 2561 within 20 calendar days of contract execution or drawing, and material direct investment inflows from non-EU controlling shareholders are subject to French Treasury statistical-reporting instructions. Funds are received into a dedicated euro or foreign-currency account, held for one to three business days for verification and negative-news screening, and released for deployment only after full sanctions, fraud, and beneficial-ownership checks have been validated.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements from the Royalty Financing Fund are executed over three complementary clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 international wire transfers for royalty advances, profit-share returns, and vendor payments, quoting the ISO 20022 purpose code and the underlying licence or invoice reference; (ii) Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit issued under UCP 600 for trade-backed vendor settlements or brand-inventory financing disbursements requiring documentary compliance; and (iii) SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for euro-denominated disbursements to EEA beneficiaries below the EUR 100,000 processing cap. Every outward payment must satisfy the EU Regulation 2015/847 data rule requiring full originator and beneficiary identification, pass the bank's sanctions and fraud filters, and obtain same-day FX pricing only after the funds are released from the escrow ledger.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable EUR/USD and EUR/GBP FX forwards with maturity up to 12 months, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with an ACPR-authorised credit institution

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in EUR/emerging-market currency pairs where the counterparty currency is non-deliverable in France, subject to internal credit approval and CMF foreign-exchange reporting where material
Cross-currency interest rate swaps hedging the SARL's non-euro financing exposure, documented under ISDA 2002 with a French FBF (Fédération Bancaire Française) credit support annex
European-style vanilla FX options for royalty cash-flow smoothing, with premium accounting and hedge documentation prepared in accordance with IFRS 9 hedge-accounting requirements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements with shareholders' approval decision (report to the AGO and allocation of profits)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce (commercial/companies register) via the INPI Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting to approve the accounts must be held within six months of the fiscal year-end; accounts deposit to the RCS within seven months after the fiscal year-end (for a 31-Dec end: meeting by 30-Jun, deposit by 31-Jul).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit: administrative fine up to €1,500 for natural persons / €7,500 for legal entities, 10% late-payment surcharge on related taxes, forced compliance by court order, and repeated non-compliance may lead to administrative strike-off (radiation) from the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liassez fiscale, forms 2065-SD and supplemental schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For an entity with a 31-Dec fiscal year-end due by 3 May of the following year; for a non-calendar year-end, within three months of the closing date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure/filing outside statutory deadline triggers a 10% increase (40% if unadjusted after formal notice, 80% if fraudulent), plus late-payment interest at 0.20% per month; company directors can be held personally liable for penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) and update of the register of beneficial owners.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI Guichet Unique / Greffe du Tribunal de commerce (for register update); register available to competent authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed at the same time as the annual accounts deposit (within seven months of the fiscal year-end); any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-disclosure or inaccurate declaration is punishable by up to six months' imprisonment and a €7,500 fine (legal entity fines up to €37,500); the company also risks cross-reference blocking on other registry filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business contribution return (cotisation foncière des entreprises — CFE) and base/valuation statement.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CFE return and settlement are filed each year by 15 June based on the prior year's situation; new taxpayers initial declarations are made on creation and by 31 December for start-ups (subject to local notices).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a 10% increase plus 0.20% per month late interest; substantive omissions subject to assessment penalties and collection enforcement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is only mandatory for SARLs exceeding at least two of the following thresholds at the balance-sheet date: total balance sheet > €25,000,000; net turnover > €50,000,000; average workforce > 250 employees during the fiscal year. For fiscal years beginning before 1 Jan 2024 lower transitional thresholds may apply.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan comptable général – PCG) as set out in ANC Regulation 2014-03; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is not required for statutory individual financial statements of a SARL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each annual financial-statement deposit, the SARL confirms and updates the register of beneficial owners held at the registered office. The confirmation is performed through the INPI Guichet Unique; any transfer or pledge of qualifying shares or control change must be declared within 30 days, and the register must reflect the current chain of ownership and control.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors/Managers (registre des gérants et décisions du gérant)
Minute Book (registre des décisions sociales / procès-verbaux d'assemblées)
Register of Beneficial Owners (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 15,000 per year if an audit is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard rate; reduced 15% for SMEs on first €42,500 of profit)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate for SMEs (turnover < €10M), research tax credit (CIR), innovation tax credit (CII), and territorial exemptions for certain activities

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (annual corporate income tax return) filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months of fiscal year-end; for calendar year-end, deadline is May 15 (or May 15+1 day if online)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification (SIREN, name, address, fiscal year)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide French tax identification number (SIREN) and permanent establishment details if applicable
Report French-source income only; apply treaty provisions for income allocation
Ensure expenses are incurred for French operations and properly documented

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (CIR, CII, foreign tax credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits available under domestic law or tax treaties

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income and tax calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply reduced rate if eligible; otherwise standard rate

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 10% of tax due (if filed within 30 days of deadline), 40% if filed after 30 days, 80% if fraudulent. Interest on late payment: 0.20% per month. Additional penalties for non-payment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2571 (quarterly corporate tax installments) filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on the 15th of March, June, September, and December (or 15th of the month following each quarter for non-calendar fiscal years)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Base on prior year's tax or current year estimate; adjust for treaty relief

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly installment amount (1/4 of annual tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay in EUR via bank transfer or direct debit

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment penalty: 0.20% per month on unpaid amount; additional 5% penalty if not paid within 30 days of notice.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (domestic law for non-resident companies; 30% for individuals under flat tax)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding tax under a tax treaty, submit Form 5000 (or Form 5001 for EU) to the French tax authority, along with a tax residency certificate (TRC) from the shareholder's country. For EU parent companies, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive may exempt withholding if the parent holds at least 10% of the subsidiary for 2 years. The application must be made before the dividend payment or within the statutory deadline for refund.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 33.33%; treaty rates often 0% or 5% (e.g., US-France 0% for certain royalties, 5% for others). Interest: statutory 30%; treaty rates often 0% or 10% (e.g., US-France 0% for certain interest, 10% for others).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €400 million (turnover or assets) for full Local File and Master File; smaller entities must maintain basic documentation (transfer pricing policy, functional analysis) if transactions exceed €1 million with related parties
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies anti-abuse rules (e.g., substance-over-form) and requires economic substance for tax residency and treaty benefits. No specific ESR regime, but entities must demonstrate real activity, staff, and decision-making in France to avoid challenges under the general anti-abuse rule (GAAR).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income, false deductions, or concealment of assets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties: up to €500,000 fine and 5 years imprisonment (Article 1741 CGI); civil penalties: 40% to 80% of tax due plus interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid taxes if they participated in fraudulent acts; travel bans and asset freezes possible

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a French entity without real economic activity, employees, or premises solely to obtain tax benefits or treaty access
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, 40% penalty for abuse of law (abus de droit), and potential criminal charges for fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for penalties and taxes if they knowingly used the entity as a sham; possible ban from managing companies

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement anti-money laundering controls, suspicious transaction reporting, or handling proceeds of crime
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million for entities; criminal penalties for directors up to 5 years imprisonment and €375,000 fine (Monetary and Financial Code)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined and imprisoned; professional disqualification and travel bans may apply

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain adequate transfer pricing documentation or applying non-arm's length prices
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, 40% penalty for serious mispricing, and interest; potential double taxation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for penalties if they knowingly approved non-compliant pricing; criminal liability for tax evasion if intentional
